name: Magasin III
funding: Robert Weil Family Foundation, funded by the Weil family office Proventus.
watch: Private museum for contemporary art in Stockholm and Jaffa.
records_note: The museum posts nothing; its funding Weil Foundation names four board members but no reports, accounts or outside donors.

name: Magazzino Italian Art
watch: Museum and research center for post-war and contemporary Italian art in Cold Spring, NY.
records_note: No annual reports found; Form 990-PFs for 2019 to 2023 are on ProPublica, no donor list is published, and trustees and advisors are named.

name: Manchester Museum
funding: University of Manchester civic endowment, UK Research & Innovation funding. Free public admission.

name: MOCA Bangkok
funding: Privately owned by DTAC telecom founder Boonchai Bencharongkul, who built it in 2012 for his collection of over 1,000 works. His son Kanachai runs it; tickets cost THB 250.
watch: Also runs a Four Seasons art space and a Suvarnabhumi airport display.
records_note: The museum site publishes no annual report, accounts, funder list or board; it presents the founder's message and its mission only.

name: Modern Art Oxford
funding: £3.1M income (FY2025). Arts Council England £909k a year, Oxford City Council £50k; Wolfson, Garfield Weston, Fidelity and other trusts; Lavazza, Edel Assanti, law firms, Oxford Brookes.
watch: No protest, boycott or flagged funder found. Oxford City Council cut its grant from £70k to £50k.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the Charity Commission register, the support page names capital funders undated, and trustees are listed.

name: Mohatta Palace Museum
funding: The Government of Sindh owns the palace, bought by the federal government after 1980. A board of trustees oversees it, and entry costs Rs 30.
watch: Opened in September 1999 with Treasures of the Talpurs. In 2021 the Sindh High Court ordered a medical college there; the government appealed.
records_note: Posts audited accounts for 2013 to 2018 and names all its trustees; no annual reports or donor list are published.

name: Mostyn
funding: £0.7M income (FY2026). Arts Council of Wales £385k, Conwy County Borough Council, Llandudno Town Council, National Gallery; Garfield Weston, Henry Moore, Ampersand, Foyle, Ashley Foundation, Mostyn Estates.
watch: Registered Welsh charity dedicated to contemporary visual art.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the Charity Commission register, the support page names partners and donors undated, and trustees are not listed.

name: mumok
funding: Federal museum funded by the Republic of Austria. Sponsors: Dorotheum, UNIQA, Gerngross, legero united. Patrons: Ludwig foundations and the Art Mentor Foundation Lucerne.
watch: Austrian federal museum situated in the MuseumsQuartier. Financial statements audited by the Austrian Court of Audit (Rechnungshof); corporate partners (Audi, Erste Bank) adhere to federal cultural patronage compliance codes.
records_note: Posts yearly culture reports and audited accounts for 2019 to 2023 and names its nine trustees; sponsors appear as undated logos.

name: Musée de la Chasse et de la Nature
funding: Private museum run by the public-interest Fondation François Sommer, set up by François and Jacqueline Sommer. A Friends association funds acquisitions.
watch: Founded in 1964 by François and Jacqueline Sommer.
records_note: Neither the museum nor Fondation François Sommer posts annual reports, accounts, a donor list or its board; only the Friends association names its own directors.

name: Museo Antropológico y de Arte Contemporáneo (MAAC)
funding: Ecuador's Culture vice-ministry (merged into Education in 2025) runs and funds it on a budget above USD 2.5M, and pays the city's Malecón 2000 foundation near USD 500,000 a year.
watch: Over 530,000 visits were counted by mid-2022. The state spent USD 451,000 on renovation in 2024 after a dispute with the city over upkeep.
records_note: No MAAC site was found, and the Culture Ministry site that runs it sits behind a bot check, so nothing could be verified.

name: Museo de la Memoria y los Derechos Humanos
funding: Government of Chile, through the national heritage service of the Ministry of Cultures: CLP 2.15 billion in 2024. A private foundation runs it.
watch: 176,846 visitors in 2024. Deputies voted down its funding in November 2022; the Senate restored it. A 3% cut hit all ministries in 2026.
records_note: Posts annual reports 2011 to 2025, financial statements 2015 to 2025 and its 15-member board; it names no sponsors, only state funding.

name: Museo de la Palabra y la Imagen (MUPI)
funding: Private non-profit. AGIAMONDO and the Ford Foundation backed its 2026 archive move; gifts from citizens, the diaspora and firms repay the annexe mortgage. Its site lists no donors or budget.
watch: Founded in 1996 and marking 30 years. Its fund drive 'Un techo para la cultura' pays for the annexe that now holds the archive.
records_note: Names its three-member board on the About page; no annual reports, accounts or donor list are published, only a donation appeal and bank details.
